objective: Integrate opencode browse (@opencode/browse 0.0.15) for Pi as a browser-use capability and add the screen capability that an Assignment carries, granting computer use, browser use and the T3 preview tools and routing that Assignment to GPT-6.1 Terra at medium or higher.
scope: Worktree /home/user/holyagent-0.3.1-screen, branch release/0.3.1/feat/screen cut from release/0.3.1/feat/fff at 3f1c135b

Intent requirements (run `holyagent intent show` is not available to you; they are quoted here): opencode browse is @opencode/browse (anomalyco/browse, MIT, 0.0.15, a stdio MCP server plus a paired Chromium extension driving the user's real browser). HolyAgent registers it as an MCP server for Pi at an exact pin, moved by deps:update, and setup reports when the extension is not installed or paired. Screen capability split: pi-computer-use for desktop apps and native browser chrome; browse for web page content in a real browser; T3 preview and HTML render tools for the page shown in T3. Computer use is not a role but a screen capability an Assignment can carry; it grants the specialist the computer-use tools (pi-computer-use), browser use (opencode browse) and the in-app browser (T3 preview tools where T3 hosts the session), and routes that Assignment to GPT-6.1 Terra whatever its role, at least medium effort. The screen capabilities are granted per Assignment to keep specialist tool lists small. Capabilities have headless and normal forms: the screen capability uses a headless Playwright Chromium in a cloud or CI session and the paired real browser and desktop computer use on a desktop; setup and doctor detect the system and pick the form, and a capability whose needs are missing is reported, not silently dropped. Cloud and headless Linux use of browse is unverified; check it from the package source and say what holds.

Existing pieces to build on: the capability registry (packages/runtime/src/config/capabilities.ts, with computer-use and mcp entries and headless/normal forms), the MCP capability and how Pi MCP servers are configured, the Pi package pin table (packages/runtime/src/config/pi-packages.json and scripts/dependency-pins.ts), the Codex route table (packages/runtime/src/pi/codex/routes.ts), the specialist launcher and agent files (packages/integrations/pi/src/agents.ts), the Assignment draft schema and dispatch in the runtime CLI, and the T3 host detection.

Read @opencode/browse 0.0.15 from npm (tarball or node_modules) to learn its MCP command, tool names, the pairing check it exposes and its platform needs; base the integration on what it actually exposes and name anything you could not confirm.
